styleMarkers.rule: The reader is the grammatical subject; abstractions do not act.
Inner states are offered with may, never asserted as diagnosis.
Alternatives are real options, not images; use no metaphor in this register.
Vary sentence length naturally and include one short, blunt sentence without turning the body into staccato fragments.
The word whether is not owner language and must not appear.
Ambient-force energy language is banned; ordinary effort-cost use remains allowed.

dailyRules.rule: Vary sentence structures across the batch; each structural function must sound independently authored.
Keep conjunction saturated, square internally frictional, opposition frictional through another person, soft mildly easier, and house fallback topic-led.
Land the close on the single concrete instruction and keep it literal to the behavior already shown.
Describe a brief available condition or friction at hours scale; results remain open.
Address the reader with respect and treat their ordinary baseline as capable.
When a room appears, use it only as a concrete collective subject in motion.
Give the body a key-specific opener construction that does not repeat another batch opener.
A room may act collectively; audience comparisons must stay attached to a named ordinary behavior.
A single instruction may naturally enumerate one person, one action, or one change without being split into extra instructions.
House fallback copy begins from its life topic, names the pull plainly, and ends at speak-up scale.
The headline makes an unhedged claim; may never appears in a headline.
The body opens inside the scene, never with a time anchor; today may appear later, sparingly.
Use may at most once in the body, and only for an inner state.
Keep the scene concrete but non-biographical; use generic current props rather than invented personal history.
The final action repairs the exact moment; no somatic or generic-wellness micro-instruction.
The ‘It takes less X to A than to B’ construction is owner-reserved; do not use it.
Use at most one quoted-dialogue line in the body, and only if it earns its place.

batch1LintGuidance.rule: Use at most one time-anchor phrase anywhere in the body, and never use it as the opener.
Use may only for a reader's inner state, never as padding on observable actions or every clause.
Match the headline grammar of the approved exemplar for this group, not only its topic or tone.
Conjunction now has approved owner exemplars; use their saturation grammar without copying their scene or phrasing.

ownerPromptCore: Draft from the lived moment, not from the astrological concept. Name what the reader is doing, what happens next, and what the behavior costs them. Replace abstract summaries with ordinary decisions, errands, messages, work, plans, money, time, and relationships. Use one concrete scene instead of listing every possible manifestation. Limit hedging. Let the headline make a clear claim in language someone would actually say. Reassurance must answer the specific fear created by the scene, not offer generic emotional permission. End with one action that directly repairs or clarifies the moment described. Vary the sentence rhythm, including at least one short, blunt sentence. Before finalizing, reject any line that could fit almost any transit or sounds like therapy, corporate training, or generic productivity advice.

ownerGuidance.rule: Find the lived moment first: the action, what immediately precedes it, the realization afterward, and its cost.
Write a headline someone would actually say: a contradiction, consequence, blunt truth, or moment already in motion.
Use one concrete scene rather than category stacks; keep it portable without listing every manifestation.
Name what becomes harder because of the pattern.
Take a position; one may or can is usually enough.
Place reassurance after recognition, and make it answer the exact shame or fear created by the scene.
Make the instruction repair the exact moment, never general wellness.
Vary sentence length and include one short, blunt turn.
Apply specificity, morning-read, and screenshot tests before returning the final JSON.

Every verb must act on an object people actually pair with it in speech. You reply to messages, not thoughts; you fix problems, not feelings. Established emotional idiom is exempt (sit with a feeling; felt, not fixed). Test each line by asking whether anyone would say it across a table. (Owner, phrase library, Jul 17 2026.)
The word 'today' appears only when it carries the meaning; the surface already says the card is about today, so elsewhere it is a crutch. (Owner, phrase library, Jul 17 2026.)

If a line would be equally true on any random day, it is not carrying the transit. Find the transit's distinctive fact and put that in the line; a passing line is checkable by tonight. (Owner, phrase library, Jul 17 2026.)

Do not open with a manufactured scene ("You ask for a ride...", "You open the calendar..."). Open closer to the conclusion ("Their good mood starts spending your time."). The lived example supports the point; it must not delay it.
When a line has a pulse, everything after it deepens or changes understanding; never interpret the line for the reader.
The ending completes the thought, not a template: a practical move, a permission, a consequence, or a recognition line. An instruction is OPTIONAL; do not end every card with an assignment.

Reassurance without a specific truth underneath is generic. First identify what happened and why the reader started doubting themselves; often no permission line is then needed. Example of stronger: "Help stops feeling generous when accepting it makes you responsible for coordinating everyone who offered."

Lived means recognizable stakes (losing income, splitting bills, repairing every relationship, preserving a broken arrangement, a boundary that inconveniences someone, needing support and not asking, a composed exterior that costs too much), not a rotation of candles, grocery runs, cafes, calendars, and group chats. A domestic scene works only when its consequence matters.
Do not build paragraphs from symmetrical opposites (This-but-that; X without Y; not A, it is B). Prefer a longer sentence carrying full context, then a blunt correction.
Make the chart-supported claim clearly; qualify only where the lived outcome genuinely varies. Never stack might/could/possible.

The headline CONTAINS the interpretation, not the subject. Sharp models: "Help can become another job when everyone arrives at once." / "The old routine is costing more time than changing it would." / "Being seen stuck may feel worse than staying stuck."

Avoid: 'You don't have to...' as recurring structure; 'This is an invitation to...'; 'For the next few hours...' inserted mechanically; 'You may notice a feeling of...'; 'There could be something...'; 'Make sure to...'; 'You already know how to do it'; 'Do it, even if you struggle'; abstract stacks; vague subconscious language; a fictional scene opening every card; a practical instruction ending every card; explaining a landed metaphor.

direct truth + lived consequence + humane understanding. Not: poetic opening + therapeutic reassurance + generic instruction. Marie names the event, power dynamic, cost, or consequence first; warmth comes after the situation is clear.

Headlines are plain conversational truths carrying the interpretation; the situation, not the reader, is usually the subject. Owner models: 'Help becomes extra work when everyone shows up at the same time.' / 'A delayed reply can make a quiet phone feel like a final verdict.' / 'Taking care of family is rarely just about the task itself.'

Bodies run in plain present indicative ('you are wondering', 'you reschedule'). Hedges live in headlines if anywhere ('can'). Do not use 'may' for what the reader is plainly doing or feeling in the scene.
Lists escalate and can carry humor: 'three offers, a meal plan, and enough enthusiasm to turn one quick errand into a full group project.' A list is a crescendo, not an inventory.
Timing details make it lived: 'within ten minutes', 'before you have even settled the first change.'

A contrast is allowed when it CORRECTS a misreading of the cost ('The weight does not just come from showing up. It comes from constantly tearing down and rearranging your life...'); still banned as mere balance (D2-6).

The closing move may be one compound instruction with two or three coordinated actions ending on a release: '...say a polite no to the rest, and move on.' Or instruction then recognition: 'Put the phone down and step away from the checkout screen. A slow reply does not get to decide what you are worth.'
Recognition lines can strip false authority from the trigger: 'A slow reply does not get to decide what you are worth.' The pattern: [small thing] does not get to [verdict verb] [what matters].

ownerFinalTests.rule: The body must fail a mechanical swap against the other thirteen batch keys; same-target sibling swaps are advisory only.
Every sentence must parse half-awake; mechanical guard caps body sentences at 28 words and flags semicolons or parentheses.
At least one body sentence must be a candidate line worth saving because it names a recognizable experience clearly.

ownerPassages.text: Blending in is not worth a first impression you do not recognize.

You dress down to blend in and leave out the one detail you actually wanted to share. Staying neutral may help you avoid attention, but it can leave you feeling invisible. Nobody can know you from the version that never shows up. Tell one person the detail you almost kept to yourself.

It’s exhausting to keep adapting just to get through a world that seems to demand you be everything to everyone. It takes real strength to keep choosing growth when staying the same would feel so much easier. Think about what your willingness to change has already asked you to let go of.

This kind of attention is a form of love that our culture barely recognizes. It's noticing that your partner always chooses the corner table at restaurants. It's remembering that your friend gets anxious in crowded spaces. It's seeing when someone is tired before they have to tell you.
And if someone’s trying to rush you? If there’s pressure to respond, to fix, to say yes before you’re ready? That’s your cue to pause.

Each of us needs to be recognized for the invisible labor of maintaining order in disorder. To be seen for the thousand micro-decisions that keep life functioning. It's human to want someone to notice that you remembered everyone's appointments, that you kept the bills paid while navigating your own storms. It's our responsibility to honor this in ourselves.
